events.title: Inaugural Meeting of the IEEE CIS London Section Chapter
events.speaker: Ruiyi Fang & Xiaoyu Ma (Western University)
events.speakerBio:
Ruiyi Fang (Chair, IEEE CIS London Section Chapter; Department of Computer Science, Western University) presented on Graph Transfer Learning — exploring how graph properties, including node attributes and structural patterns, help transfer knowledge across different graph domains.

Xiaoyu Ma (Western University) presented on Quantum AI — introducing EQE-QAOA, a framework that reduces the number of qubits needed for quantum optimization while preserving the algorithm's behavior.
events.summary: Our inaugural in-person chapter meeting introducing the newly established IEEE CIS London Section Chapter, its mission and future plans, followed by technical talks on Graph Transfer Learning and Quantum AI.
events.description:
Join us for the inaugural in-person meeting of the IEEE London Section Computational Intelligence Society (CIS) Chapter!

We introduced our newly established Chapter, its mission and future plans, followed by two technical talks:

• Graph Transfer Learning — Ruiyi Fang
Exploring how graph properties, including node attributes and structural patterns, can help transfer knowledge across different graph domains.

• Quantum AI — Xiaoyu Ma
Introducing EQE-QAOA, a framework that reduces the number of qubits needed for quantum optimization while preserving the algorithm's behavior.

Free admission; no IEEE membership required. Thank you to everyone who joined to meet the community and share ideas for future activities!

events.title: Extracting Training Data from Diffusion Language Models via Infilling
events.speaker: Dr. Yihan Wang (University of Waterloo)
events.speakerBio: Yihan Wang is a postdoctoral scholar in the Secure Systems Group, part of the Cryptography, Security, and Privacy (CrySP) Lab at the University of Waterloo, where he works with Prof. N. Asokan. He received his PhD in 2025 from the Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences. His research focuses on AI safety and trustworthy machine learning. He has published a series of works on copyright and privacy protection, as well as on the security of AI systems, in top venues including NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, and EMNLP.
events.summary: Diffusion language models generate text by filling in masked tokens using surrounding context. But could this ability expose private training data? This talk introduces infilling extraction and explores whether these models can reveal user prompts or redacted personal information, and how instruction tuning and decoding settings affect privacy risks.
events.description:
Diffusion language models (DLMs) are an emerging alternative to autoregressive LLMs. Instead of writing left to right, they fill in masked tokens in parallel at any position, using context on both sides. This makes them faster to generate and naturally suited to infilling, and they have quickly moved from research models to commercial systems. Their privacy risks, however, remain largely unexplored. Training-data extraction has so far been studied almost entirely with prefix prompts.

In this talk, Dr. Yihan Wang explores what changes when a model can fill in blanks anywhere. Dr. Wang introduces **infilling extraction**, a mask-based extraction protocol that generalizes prefix extraction, and investigates how the placement of revealed context affects extraction, whether attackers can recover user prompts or redacted personal information, whether memorization persists after instruction tuning, and how decoding settings influence information leakage.

Free admission. All are welcome!
